question.text: Compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></math>, given a tetraacetate with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>AC</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> and oxidation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Br</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> gives an acid, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math>. Reduction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HI</mi></math> gives isopentane. The possible structure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is :

solution.text:
Formation of tetraacetate with acetic anhydride means compound A has four -OH linkage. Reduction of A with HI gives isopentane i.e. molecule contains five carbon atoms.

So, C is the correct option
